claims.claim: The Left Hand of Darkness is told in a prose notable for its clarity and evocative precision.
claims.source: Encyclopedia of Science Fiction (SFE), entry 'Le Guin, Ursula K'
claims.quote: a prose notable for its clarity and evocative precision

claims.claim: Archetypal motif pairs (darkness/light, root/branch, language/silence) are woven until the motifs are the story, treated as balanced twins rather than polarities.
claims.source: Encyclopedia of Science Fiction (SFE), entry 'Le Guin, Ursula K'

claims.claim: Searoad's nonfantastic stories convey 'the same capably restrained immanence' — restraint named as a constant of her manner.
claims.source: Encyclopedia of Science Fiction (SFE), entry 'Le Guin, Ursula K'

claims.claim: Tehanu is described as a sad, powerful, quiet book about the strength of women.
claims.source: Encyclopedia of Science Fiction (SFE), entry 'Le Guin, Ursula K'

claims.claim: Le Guin avoids 'magician' (tainted by stage illusion) and coins Archmage, magelight, magewind and magery from Latin magus — none in the OED — so that the vocabulary itself resets the reader's assumptions about magic.
claims.source: Tom Shippey, 'The Magic Art and the Evolution of Words' (Hard Reading, Liverpool UP 2016; orig. Mosaic 1977) — chapter abstract

claims.claim: The magic system rests on a 'Rumpelstiltskin theory' in which every thing has a true name distinct from ordinary language, and knowing it gives power — a linguistic premise that carries plot and theme.
claims.source: Tom Shippey, 'The Magic Art and the Evolution of Words' (Hard Reading, Liverpool UP 2016; orig. Mosaic 1977) — chapter abstract

claims.claim: Kelso reads the Lathe of Heaven jellyfish sentence's four opposing blocks (two compound adjectives, two clauses) as an ocean-on-beach here-and-back rhythm that foreshadows the novel's yin/yang structure of recurrence.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, 'Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin', Paradoxa 21 (2008), pp. 7–22 (PDF)
claims.quote: rhythm at sentence level foreshadows the tenor

claims.claim: Like Yeats, Le Guin moves toward simplicity or austerity in both rhythm and content of later work; Tehanu begins in farm life and ends among a few goats and bean vines.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, 'Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin', Paradoxa 21 (2008), pp. 7–22 (PDF)
claims.quote: move toward simplicity, or at least austerity

claims.claim: In the Tenar–Moss rush-splitting scene the 'business' works as a suite of variations for pause and emphasis: the leisurely 'They split rushes for a while in silence' quickens to the snaps of 'neatly, quickly, with her nail' and is cut by the bare 'They split rushes.'
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, 'Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin', Paradoxa 21 (2008), pp. 7–22 (PDF)
claims.quote: a suite of variations to indicate pause and emphasis

claims.feature: long smooth sentence, triple repetition, assonance
claims.claim: Kalessin's arrival pairs an extraordinarily long comma-weighted sentence (weighting 'sinuous', 'claws', 'fire') with a classic triple repetition whose final word links by assonance to the previous paragraph, approaching actual poetry.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, 'Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin', Paradoxa 21 (2008), pp. 7–22 (PDF)

claims.claim: Kelso quotes Le Guin ('Collectors, Rhymesters and Drummers'): holding to the rhythm of the dragon's flight let Tehanu tell itself, and when she lost the beat she fell off and had to wait.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, 'Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin', Paradoxa 21 (2008), pp. 7–22 (PDF)

claims.claim: Rhythm analysis slides into vocabulary, 'rhythm's Siamese twin': Lathe's 'tugged hugely' and 'tidal abyss' lean embroidered, while elsewhere the same book reaches a homely simile of love made like bread.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, 'Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin', Paradoxa 21 (2008), pp. 7–22 (PDF)

claims.claim: Tehanu shows 'the skill of experience making less do more, rather than more do more' — the late style compresses.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, 'Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin', Paradoxa 21 (2008), pp. 7–22 (PDF)

claims.claim: The Language of the Night established Le Guin's lyrical, unruly and individual critical voice with 'From Elfland to Poughkeepsie' among its essays.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, 'Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin', Paradoxa 21 (2008), pp. 7–22 (PDF)
claims.quote: lyrical, unruly, and individual critical voice

claims.claim: In the Always Coming Home vision paragraph, a long opening clause checks into shortening phrases, brakes at a colon, then returns through a triple of lengthening units to a singing polysyllable ('over the Obsidian').
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, 'Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin', Paradoxa 21 (2008), pp. 7–22 (PDF)
claims.quote: Here there are no rhythmic superfluities.

verdicts.trueWording: in a prose notable for its clarity and evocative precision
verdicts.note: SFE entry fetched raw (curl, HTTP 200). Exact sentence: 'The story is told, in a prose notable for its clarity and evocative precision, as a report back to his home planet...' Every limb (Left Hand of Darkness, prose so described) on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: until it might almost be said that the motifs are the story
verdicts.note: Raw SFE page: 'shaping a story around recurrent motifs... until it might almost be said that the motifs are the story. Many of them are the simple archetypal symbols... darkness and light, root and branch, winter and summer, submission and arrogance, language and silence. These are not seen by Le Guin as polarities or opposed forces; rather, they are twin parts of a balanced whole.' All three named pairs and the twins-not-polarities limb present. Two fidelity notes, not limb failures: the SFE hedges with 'it might almost be said', and says this of the first three Hainish novels as the 'typical Le Guin strategy'.

verdicts.trueWording: conveys some of the same capably restrained immanence
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim on the raw page, of Searoad's nonfantastic Oregon-coast stories: 'Searoad: The Chronicles of Klatsand (coll 1991), assembling nonfantastic stories set on the Oregon coast, conveys some of the same capably restrained immanence.' But the page hedges ('some of the same') and applies it only backward to the Orsinia nonfantastic work; 'restrained' occurs exactly once in the whole entry (grep: 1 hit), so restraint is never named as a constant of her manner.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: restraint named as a constant of her manner — the page says only 'some of the same' immanence, of the Orsinian nonfantastic work

verdicts.trueWording: It is a sad, powerful, quiet book about the strength of women
verdicts.note: Raw SFE page, of Tehanu: The Last Book of Earthsea (1990): 'It is a sad, powerful, quiet book about the strength of women (and the ultimate impotence of Ged); it won a Nebula.' Quote and every limb present.

verdicts.trueWording: Significantly enough, it is based on a semantic point
verdicts.note: OUP live page reached raw in a real browser after the Cloudflare interstitial cleared on reload (curl 403; Wayback holds only the challenge page); the page carries the chapter's full text. Verbatim: 'Significantly enough, it is based on a semantic point'; 'a worker of magic is never described as a magician'; that term is 'deprecatory if not pejorative, a practitioner of legerdemain... rabbits up sleeves and deceptive mirrors'; 'she makes consistent use of the base-form... mage, from Latin magus; and from it she creates a series of compounds not recorded in the Oxford English Dictionary at all: Archmage, magelight, magewind, magery'; and the vocabulary limb: 'reminds them to suspend their judgement: their ideas, like their vocabulary, may be inadequate, or wrong.'

verdicts.trueWording: what one might call the 'Rumpelstiltskin theory'
verdicts.note: Same raw OUP page: 'the basic processes of magic in Earthsea depend on a concept... what one might call the Rumpelstiltskin theory. This is, that every person, place or thing possesses a true name distinct from its name in ordinary human language; and that knowing the true name, the signifiant, gives the mage power over the thing itself, the signifie.' The plot/theme limb is carried by 'expressed in many ways and at some length all the way through A Wizard of Earthsea' and 'the semantics and the explanations and the detailed apprenticeship of Ged are all necessary preparations to allow the author to approach a theme'.

verdicts.trueWording: rhythm at sentence level foreshadows the tenor of the work
verdicts.note: Kelso PDF fetched raw (HTTP 200, 16pp) and text-extracted; passage on journal pp.14-15. Verbatim: 'But in this example, rhythm at sentence level foreshadows the tenor of the work as a whole'; then 'The sentence's four opposing blocks, two compound adjectives, two clauses, echo the rhythm of ocean on beach: Here-and-back. Here-and-back' and 'the pattern of the yin/yang dynamic... this is the overall structure of Lathe of Heaven, where change occurs, and re-occurs, and re-occurs again'. Note: the yin/yang-structure reading is Kelso relaying Kathy Keating's I Ching reading.

verdicts.trueWording: Like Yeats, Le Guin does seem to move toward simplicity, or at least austerity
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, journal p.16: 'Like Yeats, Le Guin does seem to move toward simplicity, or at least austerity, in both the rhythm and content of her later work'; and 'Tehanu, on the other hand, starts in farm-life, descending at times to the edge of poverty, and the austerity of a few goats, and a patch of bean vines (251-52), is where it ends.' Fidelity note: the source hedges with 'does seem to'; the claim asserts flatly.

verdicts.trueWording: operates as a suite of variations to indicate pause and emphasis
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, journal pp.16-17 (Tenar-Moss rush-splitting quoted from Tehanu 55-56): 'the apparently trivial women's occupation of splitting rushes for baskets operates as a suite of variations to indicate pause and emphasis, which the rhythm underscores. The first leisurely, They split rushes for a while in silence, quickens to the snaps, echoing Tenar's emotion, of neatly, quickly, with her nail. Then, They split rushes, cuts this phase of the scene with a brevity...' Every limb, and the word 'business', on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: The rhythm here is almost somnambulistically smooth
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, journal p.17, of Kalessin's first arrival: 'the second sentence extraordinarily long, commas again weighting the critical words: sinuous, claws, fire. The next paragraph opens with a classic triple repetition whose final word links by assonance to the previous paragraph: her with air, and again, air. The sound device suggests how closely this approaches actual poetry.' All limbs present.

verdicts.trueWording: hold to the rhythms of the dragon's flight, the very large, long wingbeats
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, journal pp.17-18, Kelso quoting Le Guin: 'If I could hold to the rhythms of the dragon's flight, the very large, long wingbeats, then the story told itself. (Collectors, Rhymesters and Drummers, 183-84)', introduced by 'Then Le Guin describes writing Tehanu'; and on p.18 'When I lost the beat, I fell off, and had to wait ... until the dragon picked me up again. (184)'. Attribution, book and both halves confirmed.

verdicts.trueWording: discussion of vocabulary, rhythm's Siamese twin
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, journal p.14: 'close reading sentences and paragraphs, which I soon found sliding toward aesthetic judgements and discussion of vocabulary, rhythm's Siamese twin.' The examples limb is on p.15: 'the two compound adjectives and tidal abyss, tugged hugely, lean to the more embroidered, to use Yeats' term, side of vocabulary. Elsewhere Lathe reaches a contrasting simplicity: ... it has to be made, like bread' with 'the entirely homely simile'. Content fully supported; only the page cite is narrow (p.14 for the quote, p.15 for the examples).

verdicts.trueWording: the skill of experience making less do more, rather than more do more
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, journal p.16: 'At the same time, Tehanu can show the skill of experience making less do more, rather than more do more, as in the previous quote.' The gloss 'the late style compresses' is carried by the adjacent Yeats/austerity paragraph. Fidelity note: source says 'can show'.

verdicts.trueWording: establishing Le Guin's lyrical, unruly, and individual critical voice
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, journal p.8: 'The Language of the Night (1979) establishing Le Guin's lyrical, unruly, and individual critical voice with essays like From Elfland to Poughkeepsie, Science Fiction and Mrs. Brown, and Why Americans Are Afraid of Dragons.' Both limbs present.

verdicts.trueWording: Here there are no rhythmic superfluities
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, journal p.15, on the Always Coming Home vision paragraph: 'Here there are no rhythmic superfluities. The long opening clause checks into the shortening phrases... then brake to a heavy pause with the colon at see. Then the actual vision appears, returning through a triple of lengthening syntactic units to the run that ends with a singing polysyllable on a high pole over the Obsidian.' Every limb verbatim.
